subject: Learning Methods
title: What Is an SRS Algorithm
description: A micro-lesson that makes What Is an SRS Algorithm usable.

hook.text: A spaced repetition system schedules your next review at the mathematically optimal moment before you forget.

buildup.text: When you answer correctly, the interval grows. When you forget, the interval shrinks. The system adapts to you.

discovery.text: The algorithm tracks each card individually. Easy cards appear rarely. Hard cards appear often.

twist.text: You spend most of your time on material you struggle with. The system automatically focuses your effort.

climax.text: Over months, intervals grow from days to weeks to months. A mature card may only appear twice a year.

punchline.text: The algorithm remembers when you will forget.

quiz.question: What happens when you answer a card incorrectly in an SRS?
options: The card is removed from the deck
The interval shrinks and you see it again sooner
The card stays on the same schedule
